article.headline: Vertex Pharmaceuticals Climbs 4.4% To Within 1.1% Of Its 52-Week High
article.deck: Vertex is pushing out of an 11-week flat base past a 560.35 buy point, with the buy range running to 588.37.
body: Vertex Pharmaceuticals rose 23.75, or 4.4%, to 562.29 as of 1:23 p.m. Mountain, moving through the 560.35 buy point of an 11-week flat base. The base ran 13.6% deep, from a September 3 high to an October 13 low. The stock sits 0.3% past the buy point, at the bottom of a buy range that runs to 588.37. Volume is on pace for 0.61x its 50-day average, light for the session.

The 52-week high is 568.67, 1.1% above the current price. Vertex trades 7.3% above its 50-day line at 524.06 and 4.9% above its 21-day exponential average at 535.94, a reading of 0.24 ATRs from the 21-day line, so the trend is intact and not stretched. Its RS line is at a new high, and the stock ranks 84 of 99 on the desk's list. It is up 24.0% year to date and 31.8% over the past year.

The latest quarter, ended September, showed EPS of 2.56, down 39.0% from a year earlier, on revenue of 3.44 billion, up 11.8%. The three quarters before it printed EPS of 4.31, 4.02 and 4.65. The company is valued at about 142.6 billion with a forward P/E of 28.2. The next report is due February 11.
The day's headlines carry no company news; Reuters ran a factbox of major drugmaker and biotech deals on the same session Sanofi agreed to acquire Insmed.
A close back under 560.35 would put the move back inside the base.
article.watch: Whether Vertex closes above the 560.35 buy point and then clears the 568.67 52-week high.

article.headline: Insmed Jumps 14.2% On Sanofi Deal To Acquire The Respiratory Drugmaker
article.deck: Insmed is 23.5% past its 137.80 buy point and well beyond the 144.69 top of the buy range, so the entry is gone.
body: Insmed rose 21.16, or 14.2%, to 170.25 as of 1:23 p.m. Mountain after Sanofi agreed to acquire the respiratory drugmaker. Volume is on pace for 22.63x its 50-day average. The stock broke out three sessions ago, on November 19, from a 15-week cup with a 137.80 buy point; that session traded 4.67x average volume. Today's price is 23.5% past the buy point and far above the buy range, which topped at 144.69.

The cup ran 32.7% deep and formed after a bigger correction: Insmed is still 20.0% below the 212.75 high of December 2, 2025. It now trades 51.2% above its 50-day line at 112.58 and 35.5% above its 21-day exponential average at 125.63, a reading of 5.59 ATRs from the 21-day line. That is a stretched tape. The stock ranks 99 of 99 on the desk's list, though its RS line sits 23.6% below its high.

Revenue for the September quarter was 524.4 million, up 268.4% from a year earlier, and it has climbed every quarter in the table, from 263.8 million in the December 2025 quarter to 306.0 million and 425.5 million. The company still lost money: 0.46 a share in the latest quarter, after losses of 0.06, 0.76 and 1.54. Market value stands near 37.3 billion.
Barron's put the Sanofi deal at 41 billion and called it a rare win for buyer and seller.
With a buyout agreed, the stock is likely to trade on the deal terms rather than on its chart.
article.watch: How Insmed holds near 170.25 against the deal, and whether it ever revisits the 144.69 top of the buy range.

article.headline: Disney Rises Toward 52-Week High On Plan To Fold Hulu Into Disney+
article.deck: Disney is 1.7% past the 119.88 buy point of a 62-week cup and inside a buy range that runs to 125.87.
body: Disney rose 1.60, or 1.3%, to 121.87 as of 1:23 p.m. Mountain, holding the breakout it made on November 18 from a 62-week cup with a 119.88 buy point. The cup ran 23.0% deep, from an August 22, 2025, high to a March 27 low. The stock is 1.7% past the buy point and inside a buy range that reaches 125.87. Volume is on pace for 0.75x its 50-day average; the breakout session traded 2.02x average.

The 52-week high is 123.37, 1.2% above the current price. Disney trades 9.7% above its 50-day line at 111.13 and 4.0% above its 21-day exponential average at 117.21, a reading of 0.66 ATRs from the 21-day line. Four sessions after the breakout, the trend is intact and the stock is still in range. It ranks 82 of 99 on the desk's list, and its RS line is 0.6% below its high. Shares are up 7.1% this year and 16.9% over twelve months.

In the September quarter EPS rose 106.8% to 1.51 on revenue of 25.95 billion, up 15.5%. EPS across the quarters in the table ran 1.34, 1.27, 1.51 and 1.51. The forward P/E is 14.2 on a market value near 208.3 billion. The next report is due February 1.
Simply Wall St. reported that Disney plans to merge Hulu into Disney+ by December 2026, and Trefis noted the company has stopped reporting streaming profit.
A close back below 119.88 would turn this into a stalled breakout.
article.watch: Whether Disney clears the 123.37 52-week high while staying above the 119.88 buy point.

article.headline: Apple Edges Higher As Nasdaq Slides, Holds Near 52-Week High
article.deck: Apple trades 1.5% above its 345.44 buy point from a four-week flat base, inside a buy range that runs to 362.71, after bouncing off its 50-day line.
body: Apple rose 1.52, or 0.4%, to 350.60 as of 8:52 a.m. Mountain, a green print on a morning when the Nasdaq is down 2.2%. The stock broke out of a four-week flat base on Oct. 22, trading 1.17x its 50-day average volume that session. The base ran 5.7% deep from a Sept. 22 high to an Oct. 1 low of 325.81, and the buy point is 345.44. Apple sits 1.5% above it, inside the buy range that runs to 362.71. Volume is on pace for 1.09x its 50-day average.

The 52-week high is 360.83, 2.8% overhead. The stock has bounced off its 50-day line, now at 342.51, and trades 2.4% above it and 15.3% above the 200-day. It is 0.8% above the 21-day exponential line at 347.85, a reading of 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line, so the move is anything but stretched. Apple is 23 sessions past the breakout. It ranks 86 of 99 on the desk's list, and its RS line is 1.2% below its high. The stock is up 29.0% this year.

The September quarter's revenue rose 11.7% to $114.48 billion; the payload carries no EPS figure for that quarter. The June quarter's EPS of 2.02 was up 28.7%. Apple is worth about $5.10 trillion and trades at 33.2 times forward earnings. The next report is due Jan. 28, 2027.

The morning's headlines are about the broader tape rather than Apple: Yahoo Finance reported stocks giving back gains as Anthropic dipped below its IPO price. A close back under the 50-day line would undo the bounce.
article.watch: Whether Apple holds the 345.44 buy point and the 50-day line at 342.51 if the Nasdaq's slide deepens.

article.deck: Texas Instruments cut through its 50-day and 200-day lines and sits 21.4% below the 334.13 buy point of a 22-week cup, out of buyable range.
body: Texas Instruments fell 28.70, or 9.9%, to 262.49 as of 8:52 a.m. Mountain, on pace for 1.66x its 50-day average volume. The drop broke the stock's 50-day line. It is working on a 22-week cup, 25.7% deep, that topped on June 22 and bottomed at 248.13 on Sept. 3. The buy point is 334.13, and the stock now sits 21.4% below it. The handle high of 301.10 from Nov. 19 was the early entry; the stock is now 12.8% below that level.

The stock is 8.5% below its 50-day line at 286.92 and 1.7% below its 200-day at 266.94. It is 9.3% under the 21-day exponential line at 289.54, -0.49 ATRs from the 21-day line. Its 52-week high of 334.03 is 21.4% away. The stock still ranks 90 of 99 on the desk's list, but its RS line is 17.5% off its high. It is up 51.3% this year and 64.7% over a year, which leaves a lot of gain in the shares.

The business numbers don't match the chart. September-quarter EPS rose 77.0% to 2.62 and revenue grew 27.7% to $6.06 billion. EPS has climbed every quarter in the table, from 1.27 to 1.68 to 2.14 to 2.62. Texas Instruments is worth about $240.6 billion and trades at 22.4 times forward earnings. The next report is due Jan. 26, 2027.

The day's news is next door. Analog Devices sank 15% on a flat first-quarter outlook, TIKR reported, and Barron's called it the stock's worst beating since 2020. A Simply Wall St. piece the same morning looked back at an 84% rally in Texas Instruments shares.
article.watch: Whether Texas Instruments holds the Sept. 3 cup low of 248.13 or undercuts it.

article.headline: HPE Falls 12.8% Premarket As Margin Forecast Outweighs Upbeat Guidance
article.deck: The premarket print hands back all of Monday's gain and more, leaving HPE 34.8% under its 73.66 buy point in a 45% deep cup, nowhere near buyable.
body: Hewlett Packard Enterprise traded at 41.88 as of 8:50 a.m. Eastern, down 6.14, or 12.8%, from Monday's close. Yahoo Finance reported that the stock declined as a disappointing margin forecast outweighed upbeat guidance, and Wells Fargo trimmed its price target despite surging AI orders, according to a GuruFocus headline. The desk's calendar had HPE's earnings date as Nov. 23.

The drop erases Monday's move. HPE closed at 48.02 on Monday, up 7.11, or 17.4%, on volume 2.41x its 50-day average. The stock sits in a six-week deep cup, 45.0% from its Oct. 9 high to its Nov. 20 low of 40.48. The buy point is 73.66, with a buy range to 77.34; Monday's close was 34.8% below it, and the premarket price is lower still. An early entry the desk tracks, a break of the downtrend line from the Oct. 9 and Oct. 28 highs, sat at 46.47; the premarket print is under it.

The 52-week high is 73.56, and Monday's close was 34.7% off it. The stock closed 16.5% under its 50-day line at 57.51 and 3.5% under its 21-day line, with an ext_atr reading of 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line: Monday's range straddled it. The 200-day line is at 42.84, above the premarket price. HPE ranks 97 of 99 on the desk's list, but its RS line is 29.4% below its high. The stock is up 99.9% this year.

In the latest quarter in the desk's table, ended July 31, earnings rose 404.8% to 1.06 a share and revenue rose 33.7% to $12.21 billion. The three quarters before showed EPS of 0.44, 0.31 and 0.11. The forward P/E is 10.07 on a $63.7 billion market cap.
A move back over the 200-day line at 42.84 would put the stock back above its long-term trend; a break of the 40.48 low would undercut the base.
article.watch: Whether HPE holds the Nov. 20 low at 40.48 and the 200-day line at 42.84 once the session opens.

body: Analog Devices traded at 337.00 as of 8:50 a.m. Eastern, down 41.75, or 11.0%, from Monday's close. The company reported fiscal fourth-quarter results this morning: Investor's Business Daily said it topped views and gave a mixed outlook, and Investing.com reported a lower-than-expected first-quarter earnings forecast. A Stocktwits headline said the stock was on track to hit a seven-month low after a record fiscal 2026.

The gap undoes Monday's rally. ADI closed at 378.75 on Monday, up 32.83, or 9.5%, on volume 2.17x its 50-day average. The stock sits in a 22-week cup, 22.9% deep from the June 22 high to the Nov. 20 low of 343.94, with a buy point of 446.01 and a buy range to 468.31. Monday's close was 15.1% below the buy point. The premarket price is under the cup's low, which undercuts the base.

The 52-week high is 445.91. Monday's close sat 4.4% under the 50-day line at 395.99 and 2.7% under the 21-day line, at -0.02 ATRs from the 21-day line: the session's high stopped just short of it. The close was 0.1% above the 200-day line at 378.41; the premarket price is well under it. ADI ranks 78 of 99 on the desk's list, and its RS line is 12.2% off its high. The stock is up 39.7% this year and 68.2% over one year.

In the latest quarter in the desk's table, ended July 31, EPS rose 163.5% to 2.74 and revenue rose 39.6% to $4.02 billion. The three quarters before showed EPS of 2.40, 1.69 and 1.60. The Wall Street Journal reported that profit and revenue rose as industrial and data-center demand surged. The forward P/E is 23.00 on a $183.5 billion market cap.
article.watch: Whether ADI can get back above the 343.94 cup low and the 200-day line at 378.41, or the gap sets a new low for the base.

article.headline: Dell Slips 7.3% Premarket As HPE Flags Thinner AI Margins
article.deck: Dell sits 43.8% under its 595.61 buy point in a 53.9% deep cup, with earnings due today on the desk's calendar; there is no entry here.
body: Dell Technologies traded at 310.49 as of 8:50 a.m. Eastern, down 24.42, or 7.3%, from Monday's close. The overnight news belonged to a rival: HPE expects thinner AI margins, a Trefis headline said, asking whether Dell is next, and Yahoo Finance reported HPE stock declining on a disappointing margin forecast. A TIKR headline noted Dell dropped 26% in a month and that Steve Eisman warns it will slow along with Nvidia. Dell's earnings date on the desk's calendar is today, Nov. 24.

Dell closed at 334.91 on Monday, up 56.89, or 20.5%, on volume 2.09x its 50-day average. The stock sits in a nine-week deep cup, 53.9% from the Sept. 18 high to the Nov. 20 low of 274.35. The buy point is 595.61, with a buy range to 625.39; Monday's close was 43.8% below it. A correction of more than half the stock's value leaves a lot of ground to recover before the buy point matters.

The 52-week high is 595.51. Monday's close was 28.3% under the 50-day line at 467.11, 8.9% under the 21-day line, and 4.1% under the 200-day line at 349.26, reading 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line. Dell ranks 99 of 99 on the desk's list on its longer record, up 166.1% this year and 185.3% over one year, but it fell 26.6% over the past month and its RS line is 39.9% off its high.

In the latest quarter in the desk's table, ended July 31, EPS rose 272.9% to 6.34 and revenue rose 57.7% to $46.97 billion. The three quarters before showed EPS of 5.24, 3.37 and 2.28 on revenue of $43.84 billion, $33.38 billion and $27.01 billion. The forward P/E is 10.93 on a $212.9 billion market cap.
article.watch: Dell's report, due today on the desk's calendar, and whether the stock can reclaim the 200-day line at 349.26.
